messages:
sasha: thinking about adding per-API-key limits + key-level overrides for internal services/partners — want to discuss enforcement point and UX. main asks: 1) allow partner/internal keys to have higher bursts, 2) admin overrides with audit logs, 3) telemetry per-key. any concerns?

liam: sounds right. priority rules should be explicit: key-level override > org-level limit > global default. enforcement ideally at the auth gateway so we can short-circuit before routing to runtime.

chris: agree on priority. console needs an override UI (read-only history + who changed what). Also a read API so partners can query their effective limits.

ellie: burst behavior is the trickiest part. for partners we should support a token-bucket style burst_tokens + sustain_rate. if we just spike them, downstream will still be overwhelmed. need to pair with routing policies (route partner traffic to dedicated pool).

liam: +1 route to dedicated pool when key has "internal" or "partner" tag. we can store tag on key metadata and have smart routing rules. fallback: if dedicated pool full, apply org-level limit or degrade to smaller model.

sasha: telemetry needs: enforcement_point, org_id, api_key_id (hashed), route, decision (allow/deny/throttle), remaining_tokens. dashboards should let us pivot on api_key_id and alert when "throttle" spikes.

chris: UX note: don't show raw api_key_id in UI for partners. show a friendly label + hashed id. audit trail should include admin name + ip + reason.

ellie: config sketch (for implementation):

```
{
  "key_id": "key_abc123",
  "tags": ["partner", "internal"],
  "limit": { "per_minute": 1200, "burst_tokens": 300 },
  "enforcement_point": "auth-gateway",
  "override_by_role": ["platform-admin", "partner-ops"]
}
```

liam: for the API to set overrides (internal only) we can add an endpoint: POST /internal/keys/:id/override with body above. must require mTLS + audit header. example curl for internal ops: 

```
curl -X POST https://api.internal.redwood/keys/key_abc123/override \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Audit-Reason: partner onboarding spike" \
  -d '{"limit":{"per_minute":2400,"burst_tokens":800}}'
```

quota-bot: ALERT [1719001290] key=key_abc123 (partner:acme) near burst capacity: 72% used in last 30s :warning:

sasha: good catch. we should wire that alert to a partner-ops pager and add a soft quota email to partner contact. also add a graph of burst credits over time in console.

chris: implementation detail: use Redis sorted sets for per-key sliding windows or token-bucket counters with lua scripts to keep it atomic. Avoid cross-region sync; enforce at region local + global fallback.

ellie: ops/security note: only allow overriding burst_tokens for keys that have been validated (legal/data agreement). require a checklist before toggling. also we should have an emergency revoke that sets limit=0 with one click.

liam: rollout plan:
- phase 1: internal-only API + console controls behind feature flag, enforcement at auth-gateway in canary region (us-west-2)
- phase 2: add tagging + routing to dedicated pool, shadow mode to validate decisions for 48h
- phase 3: expose partner read API + managed self-serve for vetted partners

sasha: metrics to watch during rollout: rejection_rate_by_key, throttle_latency, dedicated_pool_utilization, downstream_error_rate. if rejection_rate>0.5% for internal keys we rollback.

chris: also log the effective_limit computed per request in trace (no PII). will help debug mismatch between console and runtime.

ellie: final policy thought: if override misconfigured, fallback to org-level limit and create an incident if it's > 2x difference. fail-safe beats silent unlimited keys.

sasha: ok i'll open a design PR with the config fields + API surface and console mockups. will include sample alert queries and required audit fields.

liam: thanks — I'll take the gateway changes + redis lua.

chris: I'll own console + API contract.

ellie: I'll draft partner policy + checklist.

sasha: plan looks good. tagging this for follow-up in the platform board meeting. :thumbsup:
